name: Aztreonam
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 500 mg or 1 g IV or IM every 8 or 12 hours

usual_adult_dose.indication: Severe or life-threatening infections, P. aeruginosa

key_interactions.effect: In vitro antagonism with aztreonam in some gram-negative aerobes such as Enterobacter and Pseudomonas (label).
Clinically insignificant rise in aztreonam serum levels (label).

contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to aztreonam or any component

pk.half_life_eskd: Prolonged in kidney impairment (label; no value given)
pk.excretion_renal_pct: Mainly urine, by tubular secretion and filtration about equally (label; % not given)

sources.citation: E.R. Squibb & Sons, L.L.C. (2025). AZACTAM (aztreonam for injection, USP) [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA050580, set ID 9a105eaf-ee77-4016-beeb-d425a5565db2, version effective December 15, 2025]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

draft_notes: AZACTAM has no Precautions drug-interaction subsection (checked in the FDA label PDF, NDA 50-580/S-040); interactions are from the pinned label's Indications and Clinical Pharmacology text.

revision_log.change: Interactions added from the pinned AZACTAM label: beta-lactamase inducers (cefoxitin, imipenem; do not use concurrently) and probenecid/furosemide (clinically insignificant).
Batch 6 summary approved by Dr. Rivero with the pharmacology review corrections.
